rules.title: Application
rules.summary: Defines where the steering and sailing rules apply and permits special local rules in specified waters.
rules.memory_hook: Know which rule set governs your waterway.
rules.asa_inland_note: Check whether International or US Inland Rules apply.

rules.title: Responsibility
rules.summary: Requires compliance with the rules and good seamanship, including precautions demanded by ordinary practice or special circumstances.
rules.memory_hook: The rules do not replace good seamanship.
rules.asa_inland_note: Local and Inland rules may add obligations.

rules.title: General definitions
rules.summary: Defines vessel classes, underway, making way, restricted visibility, and terms used throughout the rules.
rules.memory_hook: Classify the vessel before applying a priority rule.
rules.asa_inland_note: Use the applicable Inland definitions.

rules.title: Application of steering rules
rules.summary: Rules in this section apply in any condition of visibility.
rules.memory_hook: Rules 4–10 apply in all visibility conditions.
rules.asa_inland_note: Same broad visibility scope under Inland Rules.

rules.title: Look-out
rules.summary: Maintain a proper look-out by sight, hearing, and all available means appropriate to the prevailing conditions.
rules.memory_hook: Eyes, ears, radar, and appraisal at all times.
rules.asa_inland_note: AIS supports but does not replace a proper look-out.

rules.title: Safe speed
rules.summary: Proceed at a speed that permits effective avoiding action and stopping within an appropriate distance.
rules.memory_hook: Speed must fit visibility, traffic, and maneuverability.
rules.asa_inland_note: Assess Inland water and traffic conditions.

rules.title: Risk of collision
rules.summary: Use all available means; if in doubt, assume risk exists. Constant bearing with decreasing range is a warning.
rules.memory_hook: CBDR means collision risk.
rules.asa_inland_note: Use radar plotting when available.

rules.title: Action to avoid collision
rules.summary: Take positive, timely action; make alterations large enough to be apparent and verify their effect.
rules.memory_hook: One bold, early alteration beats tiny successive changes.
rules.asa_inland_note: Signal intent as required by the applicable rules.

rules.title: Narrow channels
rules.summary: Keep to the starboard outer limit when safe and practicable; small vessels and sailing vessels must not impede a vessel confined to the channel.
rules.memory_hook: Keep right; do not impede a channel-bound vessel.
rules.asa_inland_note: Some Inland provisions address downbound vessels with a following current.

rules.title: Traffic separation schemes
rules.summary: Follow the traffic flow, cross lanes nearly at right angles, and avoid impeding vessels using a lane.
rules.memory_hook: Cross at right angles on heading, not merely COG.
rules.asa_inland_note: Check designated Inland traffic schemes and local rules.

rules.title: Application of sailing rules
rules.summary: Rules 11–18 apply to vessels in sight of one another.
rules.memory_hook: In sight: apply the encounter rules.
rules.asa_inland_note: Use the Inland definition of in sight.

rules.title: Sailing vessels
rules.summary: Sets give-way action between sailing vessels based on tack and windward position, with a special uncertainty rule.
rules.memory_hook: Port tack gives way; windward gives way when on the same tack.
rules.asa_inland_note: The sailing-vessel hierarchy is materially the same.

rules.title: Overtaking
rules.summary: An overtaking vessel keeps clear until finally past and clear; doubt is resolved in favor of being overtaking.
rules.memory_hook: The vessel coming from astern keeps clear.
rules.asa_inland_note: Maintain the overtaking duty until past and clear.

rules.title: Head-on situation
rules.summary: Power-driven vessels meeting on reciprocal or nearly reciprocal courses alter to starboard to pass port-to-port when safe.
rules.memory_hook: Head-on: both alter to starboard.
rules.asa_inland_note: Sound-signal intent rules can differ Inland.

rules.title: Crossing situation
rules.summary: The power-driven vessel with the other on her starboard side keeps out of the way and avoids crossing ahead if circumstances permit.
rules.memory_hook: Traffic on your starboard side: keep clear.
rules.asa_inland_note: Apply the specific Inland signal requirements.

rules.title: Action by give-way vessel
rules.summary: The give-way vessel takes early and substantial action to keep well clear.
rules.memory_hook: Give-way means act early and clearly.
rules.asa_inland_note: Use the applicable Inland sound signals.

rules.title: Action by stand-on vessel
rules.summary: The stand-on vessel maintains course and speed initially, but may act as danger develops and must act when the give-way vessel fails.
rules.memory_hook: Stand on first; escalate when collision cannot be avoided.
rules.asa_inland_note: The duty to avoid collision remains paramount.

rules.title: Responsibilities between vessels
rules.summary: Allocates responsibilities among power-driven, sailing, fishing, restricted-maneuverability, and constrained vessels.
rules.memory_hook: Identify vessel status, then apply the hierarchy.
rules.asa_inland_note: Check definitions and special Inland provisions.

rules.title: Conduct in restricted visibility
rules.summary: Proceed at safe speed, use engines ready, and take cautious avoiding action; do not turn to port for a target forward of the beam except when overtaking.
rules.memory_hook: Fog: no stand-on vessel; forward target means no port turn.
rules.asa_inland_note: Rules 11–18 do not govern vessels not in sight.

rules.title: Application of lights and shapes
rules.summary: Specifies when lights must be displayed and when prescribed shapes are shown by day.
rules.memory_hook: Know when lights and shapes apply.
rules.asa_inland_note: Check visibility and local light requirements.

rules.title: Definitions of lights
rules.summary: Defines masthead, sidelights, sternlight, towing light, all-round light, and flashing light.
rules.memory_hook: Learn arcs and names before identifying a vessel.
rules.asa_inland_note: Use the prescribed characteristics in the applicable rule set.

rules.title: Visibility of lights
rules.summary: Sets minimum light ranges according to vessel length and light type.
rules.memory_hook: Vessel length controls minimum visibility range.
rules.asa_inland_note: Use charted or local requirements where applicable.

rules.title: Power-driven vessels underway
rules.summary: Prescribes masthead, sidelights, and sternlight for power-driven vessels underway, with length-based exceptions.
rules.memory_hook: Power-driven underway: masthead, sidelights, stern.
rules.asa_inland_note: Review Inland-specific light provisions.

rules.title: Towing and pushing
rules.summary: Prescribes lights and shapes for towing and pushing arrangements, including long tows.
rules.memory_hook: Tow length changes the towing vessel's signals.
rules.asa_inland_note: Check Inland differences for towing lights.

rules.title: Sailing vessels underway and vessels under oars
rules.summary: Prescribes sailing-vessel lights and permits optional all-round lights; a motor-sailing vessel displays the power-driven signal.
rules.memory_hook: Sail plus engine engaged is treated as power-driven.
rules.asa_inland_note: Check local recognition and motor-sailing practice.

rules.title: Fishing vessels
rules.summary: Prescribes lights and shapes for fishing vessels, distinguishing trawling from other fishing.
rules.memory_hook: Trawling: green over white; fishing: red over white.
rules.asa_inland_note: Recognize fishing status and keep clear as required.

rules.title: Vessels not under command or restricted in ability to maneuver
rules.summary: Prescribes signals for NUC and RAM vessels, including red-white-red lights and day shapes for RAM.
rules.memory_hook: NUC: red over red; RAM: red-white-red.
rules.asa_inland_note: Use the defined status and prescribed signals.

rules.title: Vessels constrained by their draught
rules.summary: Allows a power-driven vessel constrained by her draught to display three all-round red lights or a cylinder in addition to normal lights.
rules.memory_hook: Constrained by draft: three reds and cylinder.
rules.asa_inland_note: Keep clear when the vessel's constrained status is apparent.

rules.title: Pilot vessels
rules.summary: Prescribes white over red lights for a pilot vessel on duty, with normal underway lights as applicable.
rules.memory_hook: White over red: pilot ahead.
rules.asa_inland_note: Confirm pilot status and local communications.

rules.title: Anchored vessels and vessels aground
rules.summary: Prescribes anchor lights and shapes; vessels aground add the required signals.
rules.memory_hook: Anchored: all-round white; aground adds red and balls.
rules.asa_inland_note: Observe local anchoring and harbor requirements.

rules.title: Seaplanes
rules.summary: Requires a seaplane to display lights and shapes as closely similar to the rules as circumstances permit.
rules.memory_hook: Aircraft on water follow the closest practicable signals.
rules.asa_inland_note: Apply aviation and local waterway provisions as relevant.

rules.title: Definitions of sound signals
rules.summary: Defines short blast and prolonged blast durations for sound-signal rules.
rules.memory_hook: Short: about one second; prolonged: four to six seconds.
rules.asa_inland_note: Signal duration follows the prescribed definitions.

rules.title: Equipment for sound signals
rules.summary: Sets whistle, bell, and gong equipment requirements according to vessel length.
rules.memory_hook: Required sound equipment depends on vessel length.
rules.asa_inland_note: Check Inland equipment requirements.

rules.title: Manoeuvring and warning signals
rules.summary: Prescribes whistle signals for maneuvering and warning when vessels are in sight of one another.
rules.memory_hook: One short: altering to starboard internationally.
rules.asa_inland_note: Inland Rule 34 assigns different passing-signal intent in some situations.

rules.title: Sound signals in restricted visibility
rules.summary: Prescribes fog signals for vessels underway, stopped, sailing, fishing, constrained, or at anchor.
rules.memory_hook: Learn the fog-signal pattern by vessel status.
rules.asa_inland_note: Use the applicable Inland sound-signal requirements.

rules.title: Signals to attract attention
rules.summary: Permits attention signals that cannot be mistaken for a prescribed signal or impair another vessel's lookout.
rules.memory_hook: Attract attention without confusion or hazard.
rules.asa_inland_note: Avoid signals that could be mistaken for distress or maneuvering signals.

rules.title: Distress signals
rules.summary: Requires a vessel using or observing a distress signal to act in accordance with Annex IV and applicable duties.
rules.memory_hook: Recognize distress and respond promptly.
rules.asa_inland_note: Use USCG distress procedures and available rescue channels.

rules.title: Exemptions
rules.summary: Provides limited exemptions for certain vessels built or converted before specified dates.
rules.memory_hook: Exemptions are narrow and date-dependent.
rules.asa_inland_note: Verify the vessel's documented exemption and local applicability.

rules.title: Training and qualification
rules.summary: Reference note for training users: verify current national competency and qualification requirements separately.
rules.memory_hook: Training requirements are not a substitute for the rules of the road.
rules.asa_inland_note: Confirm current USCG and ASA qualification guidance.

rules.title: Local supplements
rules.summary: Reference note to check local navigation, port, and authority supplements before a passage.
rules.memory_hook: Local rules can supplement the collision regulations.
rules.asa_inland_note: Check Inland and state/local navigation rules.

rules.title: Reference and revision note
rules.summary: Study index entry retained for the requested 72-entry reference; consult the official current rule text for legal application.
rules.memory_hook: Use the official publication for authoritative rule text.
rules.asa_inland_note: Verify current official Inland and International publications.

rules.title: Positioning and technical details of lights and shapes
rules.summary: Provides technical details for positioning, spacing, and screening of lights and shapes.
rules.memory_hook: Use Annex I for installation geometry.
rules.asa_inland_note: Check vessel-specific light installation requirements.

rules.title: Additional signals for fishing vessels
rules.summary: Adds signals for fishing vessels operating in close proximity and other relevant fishing conditions.
rules.memory_hook: Annex II adds fishing signals to Rule 26.
rules.asa_inland_note: Check local fisheries and Inland signal provisions.

rules.title: Technical details of sound signal appliances
rules.summary: Specifies technical characteristics of whistles, bells, gongs, and sound signal equipment.
rules.memory_hook: Annex III covers sound equipment specifications.
rules.asa_inland_note: Use approved equipment for the vessel class.

rules.title: Distress signals
rules.summary: Lists recognized distress signals, including radio, visual, and sound indications.
rules.memory_hook: Distress signals mean grave and imminent danger.
rules.asa_inland_note: Use current USCG distress and emergency procedures.

rules.title: General application
rules.summary: The rules apply to vessels on the high seas and connected navigable waters used by seagoing vessels.
rules.memory_hook: Confirm the waterway falls within scope.
rules.asa_inland_note: Inland Rules govern designated US waters.

rules.title: Ordinary practice
rules.summary: Nothing in the rules exonerates a vessel from neglecting precautions required by ordinary seamanship.
rules.memory_hook: Compliance includes ordinary seamanship.
rules.asa_inland_note: Apply prudent seamanship in addition to Inland Rules.

rules.title: Vessel definition
rules.summary: A vessel includes every description of watercraft used or capable of being used as a means of transportation on water.
rules.memory_hook: A broad definition: watercraft used on water.
rules.asa_inland_note: Check definitions for specialized craft.

rules.title: Visibility scope
rules.summary: The all-visibility steering rules include look-out, safe speed, collision risk, avoiding action, channels, and traffic separation schemes.
rules.memory_hook: Rules 4–10 are your all-visibility baseline.
rules.asa_inland_note: Apply all-visibility rules Inland as well.

rules.title: Look-out by all means
rules.summary: Use sight, hearing, and every appropriate available means to appraise the situation and risk of collision.
rules.memory_hook: Detection plus appraisal, continuously.
rules.asa_inland_note: AIS does not replace lookout by sight and hearing.

rules.title: Safe speed factors
rules.summary: Consider visibility, traffic density, maneuverability, background lights, wind, sea, current, hazards, and draft.
rules.memory_hook: Speed is a conditions-based decision.
rules.asa_inland_note: Include local traffic and current conditions.

rules.title: Assume risk when in doubt
rules.summary: If there is any doubt whether risk of collision exists, the vessel shall deem that risk to exist.
rules.memory_hook: Doubt means risk exists.
rules.asa_inland_note: Use radar plotting and systematic observation.

rules.title: Positive avoiding action
rules.summary: Action to avoid collision shall be positive, made in ample time, and with due regard to good seamanship.
rules.memory_hook: Positive, early, and apparent.
rules.asa_inland_note: Make signals that fit the Inland encounter rules.

rules.title: Narrow-channel position
rules.summary: A vessel proceeding along a narrow channel keeps as near to the starboard outer limit as is safe and practicable.
rules.memory_hook: Keep to the starboard side when safe.
rules.asa_inland_note: Account for current, channel marks, and local directions.

rules.title: Traffic lane direction
rules.summary: A vessel using a traffic separation scheme proceeds in the appropriate lane in the general direction of traffic flow.
rules.memory_hook: Join the lane in its direction of flow.
rules.asa_inland_note: Follow the scheme's charted direction and local rules.

rules.title: Vessels in sight
rules.summary: The steering and sailing rules for vessels in sight apply when one vessel can be observed visually from the other.
rules.memory_hook: Visual sighting activates Rules 11–18.
rules.asa_inland_note: Do not treat radar-only contact as being in sight.

rules.title: Sailing-vessel tack
rules.summary: When sailing vessels approach, the vessel with wind on port tack keeps out of the way, subject to the rule's exceptions.
rules.memory_hook: Port tack gives way to starboard tack.
rules.asa_inland_note: Assess tack and uncertainty carefully.

rules.title: Overtaking sector
rules.summary: A vessel is overtaking when approaching from more than 22.5 degrees abaft another vessel's beam.
rules.memory_hook: Recognize the stern sector before passing.
rules.asa_inland_note: When uncertain, assume overtaking.

rules.title: Reciprocal courses
rules.summary: A power-driven vessel meeting another on reciprocal or nearly reciprocal courses alters to starboard.
rules.memory_hook: Head-on: both go right.
rules.asa_inland_note: Inland passing signals may specify intent.

rules.title: Crossing with vessel to starboard
rules.summary: The vessel that has the other on her own starboard side keeps out of the way.
rules.memory_hook: If the other is on your starboard, give way.
rules.asa_inland_note: Avoid crossing ahead where circumstances permit.

rules.title: Give-way action
rules.summary: Every give-way vessel takes early and substantial action to keep well clear.
rules.memory_hook: Do not wait until close quarters.
rules.asa_inland_note: Communicate intent using the proper signals.

rules.title: Stand-on escalation
rules.summary: The stand-on vessel may act when it becomes apparent the give-way vessel is not taking appropriate action.
rules.memory_hook: Stand-on is not permission to collide.
rules.asa_inland_note: Act decisively when the other vessel fails to give way.

rules.title: Power-driven vessel duties
rules.summary: A power-driven vessel underway keeps out of the way of specified vessels not under command, restricted, fishing, or sailing.
rules.memory_hook: Know the vessel classes and order.
rules.asa_inland_note: Interpret status using the applicable definitions.

rules.title: Restricted visibility baseline
rules.summary: This rule applies to vessels not in sight of one another when navigating in or near restricted visibility.
rules.memory_hook: Radar-only contact is not a stand-on encounter.
rules.asa_inland_note: Proceed with caution and safe speed.

rules.title: Night and restricted visibility
rules.summary: Rules for lights apply from sunset to sunrise and during restricted visibility, with specified exceptions.
rules.memory_hook: Lights are required at night and in restricted visibility.
rules.asa_inland_note: Follow local lighting requirements and exemptions.

rules.title: Masthead light
rules.summary: A masthead light is a white light over the fore-and-aft centerline showing an unbroken arc of 225 degrees.
rules.memory_hook: Masthead light: white, forward arc 225 degrees.
rules.asa_inland_note: Know the visibility arc when identifying aspect.

rules.title: Light range
rules.summary: Minimum range requirements vary with vessel length and whether the light is a masthead, sidelight, or sternlight.
rules.memory_hook: Length determines the required range.
rules.asa_inland_note: Use the current vessel equipment rules.

rules.title: Power-driven underway lights
rules.summary: A power-driven vessel underway displays a masthead light, sidelights, and sternlight, subject to permitted exceptions.
rules.memory_hook: Identify the white masthead light and colored sidelights.
rules.asa_inland_note: Review exceptions for small vessels and Inland waters.

rules.title: Tow length
rules.summary: A vessel towing astern displays prescribed towing lights; a tow longer than 200 m requires additional signals.
rules.memory_hook: Tow length changes the light stack and shapes.
rules.asa_inland_note: Measure the tow and check Inland variants.

rules.title: Sailing-vessel lights
rules.summary: A sailing vessel underway displays sidelights and a sternlight; optional all-round lights may also be used.
rules.memory_hook: Sailing vessel: sidelights and sternlight.
rules.asa_inland_note: An engine-engaged motor-sailing vessel displays power-driven lights.

rules.title: Fishing-vessel lights
rules.summary: A vessel engaged in fishing displays the lights and shapes indicating fishing activity and whether it is trawling.
rules.memory_hook: Red-white fishing; green-white trawling.
rules.asa_inland_note: Fishing status does not remove every collision duty.

rules.title: NUC and RAM signals
rules.summary: NUC and RAM vessels display prescribed all-round lights and shapes to indicate their restricted ability to maneuver.
rules.memory_hook: NUC two red; RAM red-white-red.
rules.asa_inland_note: Keep clear when status is apparent.
